unit.title: Assemble & disassemble scaffolding to enable access to the work area

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Your team must weld brackets to a steel column 5 m up in the shop. Why is a scaffold or tower usually a better choice than a ladder for this job?
options: A ladder costs less to buy and to store
It gives a guarded platform, so both hands are free
A scaffold never needs checking before use
Welding is not allowed within 2 m of a ladder

questions.stem: Under the Centre's rules, who may erect, alter or take down a scaffold?
options: Any trainee who has watched it being done once
The person who needs to use it that day
Anyone, as long as a supervisor is nearby
Only people trained and authorised to do it

questions.stem: Before a tower scaffold is put up beside a structure, which ground condition must be checked first?
options: That it is firm and level enough for the base
That it has a painted non-slip coating laid on it
That it is close to the welding machine
That it has been swept clean that morning

questions.stem: What is the job of a sole board placed under a scaffold base plate on soft ground?
options: To raise the scaffold to the height of the job
To stop the bottom of the scaffold from rusting
To spread the load so the leg does not sink
To let the scaffold roll along more easily

questions.stem: On a tube-and-fitting scaffold, what are the upright tubes called?
options: Ledgers
Transoms
Standards
Diagonal braces

questions.stem: Why must each standard sit squarely in the middle of its base plate?
options: So the load goes straight down and the leg cannot slip
So the base plate does not rust under the tube
So the whole scaffold can be rolled about more easily on site
So the standard can be welded to the base plate

questions.stem: Which coupler is used to join two scaffold tubes at an angle other than 90°?
options: A right-angle coupler
A sleeve coupler
A putlog coupler
A swivel coupler

questions.stem: Another trade has taken out one brace on a scaffold to get pipes through. What should happen?
options: Carry on, as one brace makes little difference
Tag it unsafe until a trained person puts it right
Tie the gap with rope and use it with care
Weld a flat bar across the gap in its place

questions.stem: While sorting parts before putting up a tower, you find a frame with a cracked weld and a bent brace. What should you do?
options: Weld the crack and straighten the brace yourself
Use them low down, where the loads are smaller
Use them, as one small crack will not matter
Tag them as faulty and keep them out of use

questions.stem: Before anyone climbs a mobile tower scaffold, what must be done with its castors?
options: Oil them so that they turn freely
Lock all the castor brakes
Take them off the bottom of the legs
Turn them all to face outwards

questions.stem: Why are outriggers (stabilisers) fitted to a mobile tower scaffold?
options: To give a place to stand the gas cylinders
To build the tower higher than its frames allow
To widen the base so the tower is more stable
To lift the tower over steps and kerbs

questions.stem: How high may a mobile tower be built on a given base size?
options: Only as high as the maker's instructions allow
As high as the frames on site will reach
Up to twice the height of the person who is using it
To any height, if a ladder is tied to it

questions.stem: A mobile tower must be moved 10 m along the shop floor. What is the right way to do it?
options: Everyone and all tools off, then push it at the base
Two people stay on top to hold the tools as it moves
Pull it along from the top rail with a long rope
Move it fast so that it has no time to tip over

questions.stem: Which edge protection should a working platform have wherever a person could fall from it?
options: A single rope at knee height
A painted line along the edge
A top rail, a mid rail and toe boards
A sign saying 'Keep away from the edge'

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the toe board on a scaffold platform?
options: To give the worker a raised step to stand on
To stop tools and materials falling off
To hold the platform boards together
To keep the sun off the worker's feet

questions.stem: Why must platform boards be fully supported, with no wide gaps between them?
options: So the boards look neat when inspected
So paint and slag can drop through the gaps
So the boards can be used again later
So nobody trips or drops tools through

questions.stem: How should a worker get onto the platform of a tower scaffold?
options: By climbing up the outside of the end frame
By the built-in ladder or stair inside it
By standing on a drum to reach the top
By climbing the braces at the corners

questions.stem: A ladder is used to reach a scaffold platform. Which set-up is correct?
options: Leaning at a shallow angle, with no ties
Resting on a welding machine to gain height
Stopping well below the level of the platform
Tied, 1 out for every 4 up, 1 m above the landing

questions.stem: When a frame scaffold is erected, why is the bottom lift levelled and squared before going any higher?
options: Errors at the base get worse as it rises
The upper lifts can then be left out of level
It makes the scaffold quicker to take down
Levelling matters only for the top platform

questions.stem: Why should the guardrails be fitted at each level before anyone works on that level?
options: Guardrails make the platform boards stiffer
Guardrails give a place to hang welding leads
Workers on that level are then protected from falls
They are easier to fit at the end of the job

questions.stem: Under the Centre's rules, when must a worker wear a full-body harness while erecting a scaffold?
options: Only when the supervisor is watching the job
Never, because a harness gets in the way
Where guardrails are not yet in and the rules require it
Only on scaffolds that are painted yellow

questions.stem: Where should a harness lanyard be clipped?
options: To a strong anchor point that the plan approves
To the toe board along the edge of the platform
To the belt loops on the worker's own trousers
To the welding cable, as it is close by

questions.stem: A tall scaffold is built against a building. Why is it tied to the building?
options: To stop the building from moving in wind
To hold the platform boards in place
To carry the welding leads up the side
To stop it toppling or pulling away

questions.stem: Why must you not stack a heavy pile of steel plate on a light-duty scaffold platform?
options: The platform will get dirty and slippery
It may overload the boards and the scaffold
The plate will rust faster when it is stored up high
It makes the scaffold harder to inspect

questions.stem: You arrive at a scaffold and the tag at its access point shows it is not safe to use. What should you do?
options: Use it carefully and stay close to the ladder
Climb up and check it over yourself first
Use it only for short jobs of a few minutes
Keep off it and report to the supervisor

questions.stem: What does a current, signed inspection tag at a scaffold's access point tell the users?
options: Who owns the scaffold and how much it cost
It has been inspected and is safe to use
How many people put the scaffold up
That anyone may now alter the scaffold

questions.stem: After a night of heavy rain and strong wind, what should happen before an outdoor scaffold is used again?
options: Nothing, as it was inspected last week
Wipe the boards dry and start working
A competent person inspects it again
Add extra boards on top for weight

questions.stem: What should an inspector check at the base of a scaffold?
options: Plates and sole boards in place, ground not sunk or washed out
That the base plates are all painted the same colour
That the ground is dry enough for workers to sit on
That the welding machine is parked right beside it

questions.stem: Why must a welder never clamp the welding return lead to the scaffold?
options: Current could flow through tubes and couplers
The scaffold will rust at the spot where the clamp is fixed
The clamp would scratch the scaffold paint
The arc would be harder to strike that way

questions.stem: You will weld from a scaffold that has timber boards. Which fire precaution matters most?
options: Soak the boards in oil to keep them cool
Weld fast so the boards have no time to heat
Fire blankets on the boards, a fire watch, an extinguisher
Wipe the boards over with thinners first

questions.stem: Where should the oxy-fuel cylinders be kept when a welder is cutting from a scaffold platform?
options: Laid flat on the platform near the work
Upright and secured on the ground, clear of the work
Tied to the rungs of the access ladder
Hung from the guardrail on a strong rope

questions.stem: Why must nobody weld or cut on scaffold tubes, frames or couplers?
options: It wastes welding rods, wire and gas
It makes the scaffold look untidy
It spoils the paint on the frames
It can weaken parts that carry load

questions.stem: A tower must be put up near overhead power lines outside the shop. What should be done?
options: Build it quickly and keep low on the platform
Stop and get advice from the power company and Centre
Use timber boards so the tower cannot conduct
Wear rubber gloves while the tower is erected

questions.stem: Why is the area around a scaffold that is being erected or taken down barricaded and signed?
options: To keep the parts stored out of the rain
To stop the scaffold being stolen
To keep slag off the floor below
To keep people clear of falling parts

questions.stem: In what order is a scaffold normally taken down?
options: The reverse of erection, from the top down
Base plates first, then working upwards
All the braces first, then everything else
Any order, as long as it is done quickly

questions.stem: How should scaffold parts be brought down from height during dismantling?
options: Thrown clear onto a soft heap of sand
Dropped, after a warning is shouted below
Passed down by hand or lowered on a line
Slid down the outside of the frames

questions.stem: During dismantling, when may the guardrails at a level be taken off?
options: First of all, so the parts are easier to reach
As soon as the scaffold tag has been removed
Only as that level comes down, as the method says
At any time, as long as it is not windy

questions.stem: After dismantling, how should scaffold parts be stored?
options: Sorted, checked for damage and racked off the ground
Piled in one heap in the yard ready for next time
Left where they were dropped until the next job
Stacked up against the sides of the welding booths outside

questions.stem: Strong wind is forecast while your team is using an outdoor tower. What should the team leader do?
options: Fix plywood sheets to the sides to block the wind
Keep working but tell everyone to hold the rail
Build the tower higher so the job finishes sooner
Check the maker's wind limit and stop work if passed

questions.stem: Which details should a scaffold plan give before erection starts?
options: Only the colour of the frames to be used
Type, height, loads, base, ties and who erects it
The name of the client's bank and account
The break times and music for the crew

questions.stem: A trainee on your team starts to climb a tower that has no tag on it. What should you do as team leader?
options: Let him go, since he is only going up very briefly
Ask him to bring the tag down with him
Hold the tower steady while he climbs up
Stop him and have the tower inspected first

questions.stem: How should the boards at the end of a platform be placed?
options: With a long overhang to make the platform a bit longer
Supported properly, with no long unsupported ends
Resting on the guardrail at one end only
With gaps between them so rain runs through

questions.stem: What is an adjustable base jack used for on a frame scaffold?
options: To join two frames together end to end
To lift the scaffold up onto a truck
To level the scaffold on uneven ground
To lock the castors so they cannot turn

questions.stem: Why should a scaffold team agree clear words or signals before passing parts up and down?
options: So each knows when to take or let go of a part
So the crew can work without wearing hard hats
So the supervisor no longer needs to be there
So the parts can be thrown instead of passed

questions.stem: Which PPE does everyone erecting a scaffold need?
options: Hard hat, safety boots and gloves; harness if required
A welding helmet and a leather apron only
Ear muffs and a paper dust mask only
Sandals, so their feet grip the boards

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the horizontal tube that runs along the length of a scaffold, joining the standards?
What is the name of the short tube that crosses the width of a scaffold and carries the platform boards?
What is the name of the piece of timber placed under a base plate to spread the load on soft ground?
What is the name of the board fixed upright along the edge of a platform to stop tools being kicked off?
A ladder rises 4 m to a platform. How far out from the base of the wall should its foot be, in metres?
What is the name of the fitting used to join two scaffold tubes end to end?
What equipment, worn on the body and connected by a lanyard to an anchor, stops a worker's fall?
What is the name of the label at a scaffold's access point that shows whether it has been inspected and may be used?
What part of each castor on a mobile tower must be locked before anyone climbs it?
What is the name for the height from one level of ledgers to the next on a scaffold?
What is the name for the person who watches for fire during and after welding or cutting on a scaffold?
How many points of contact should a person keep with a ladder while climbing it?
What is the name of the fixing that holds a scaffold to a building or structure so it cannot pull away or topple?
What do we call the barricaded area around a scaffold that people must not enter while it is put up or taken down?
What is the name of the diagonal tube that stops a scaffold from swaying?

essays.stem: Your team must weld a steel canopy to a building wall, 4 m above a concrete yard. Explain how you would plan safe access by scaffold for this job.
essays.modelAnswer: I start by looking at the job and the site: the height, the length of the canopy, the ground, any overhead lines, traffic and other trades nearby. I choose the type of scaffold, for example a frame scaffold or mobile towers along the wall, big enough to carry the welders, their tools and a short length of steel. I check the maker's instructions for height, base size, outriggers and loads, and whether ties to the wall are needed. I arrange for the scaffold to be erected only by trained, authorised people and inspected and tagged before use. I plan fall protection: full guardrails and toe boards, and harnesses where the rules require them. Because we are welding, I plan the hot work: fire blankets, a fire watch, an extinguisher, gas cylinders kept on the ground and return leads clamped to the work, never the scaffold. I mark an exclusion zone below and record the plan.
markingPoints: Surveys the site: height, ground, overhead lines, traffic
Chooses a suitable scaffold type and checks maker's limits and loads
Erection by trained, authorised people; inspection and tag before use
Plans fall protection and an exclusion zone below
Plans hot-work precautions specific to welding from a scaffold

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how a trained team would erect a mobile aluminium tower scaffold, following the maker's instructions.
essays.modelAnswer: The team reads the maker's instructions and checks that all the parts are there and in good condition, with no bent tubes, cracked welds or faulty brakes or clips. They check the ground is firm and level and clear of overhead hazards, and set up an exclusion zone. They fit the castors and lock the brakes, then fit the base frames and the horizontal and diagonal braces in the order the maker shows. They check the base is level, using the adjustable legs, and fit the outriggers. They build up frame by frame, fitting braces as they go, and fit the platforms. Guardrails are fitted from the protected level below, or using the maker's advance guardrail method, before anyone stands on a new level. Toe boards are fitted at the working platform. They check the height is within the limit for the base and outriggers. Finally a competent person inspects the tower and puts on the inspection tag.
markingPoints: Reads the instructions and checks all parts before starting
Checks ground, overhead hazards and sets an exclusion zone
Locks castors, levels the base and fits outriggers
Builds in the correct order with braces, platforms and guardrails before standing on each level
Checks height limit, fits toe boards, inspects and tags before use

essays.stem: Explain how you would check scaffold components before they are used, and what you would do with any that are faulty.
essays.modelAnswer: Before erection the parts are laid out and checked one by one. Tubes and frames are checked for bends, dents, splits, cracked welds and heavy rust, and that their ends are square. Couplers are checked for cracks, worn or bent bolts and threads that do not run freely, and they are cleaned and oiled as the maker says. Base plates and base jacks are checked for bends and stiff threads. Timber boards are checked for splits, rot, large knots, warping and burn marks, and their end bands must be in place; metal boards are checked for dents and broken hooks. Ladders, castors and brakes are checked for damage. Any faulty part is tagged or painted as faulty, put in a separate quarantine area, and reported, so that it cannot be used by mistake. It is repaired only by a competent person, or scrapped. A tradesperson must never weld a scaffold part to repair it.
markingPoints: Checks tubes and frames for bends, cracks and rust
Checks couplers, base plates and jacks for damage and free threads
Checks boards, ladders and castors
Tags and quarantines faulty parts and reports them
Repairs only by a competent person or scraps; never welds scaffold parts

essays.stem: Explain how a scaffold inspection and tag system works: when inspections are done, who does them, what is checked and how the tags are used.
essays.modelAnswer: A scaffold is inspected by a competent person before it is first used, after any alteration, after anything that could affect it, such as high wind, heavy rain or an impact, and at the regular intervals the Centre's rules set, often weekly. The inspector checks the base and ground, the standards, ledgers, transoms and braces, the couplers, the ties, the platform boards, the guardrails and toe boards, and the access ladder, and that the scaffold suits the load and the job. The result is written in the inspection register. A tag at each access point shows its status: one side or colour shows it has been inspected and is safe to use, with the date and the inspector's signature; another shows it is not to be used. Users must look at the tag every time before they climb. If there is no tag, or it shows unsafe, or the date is out, nobody uses the scaffold and it is reported.
markingPoints: Inspected before first use, after alteration or bad weather, and at set intervals
Done by a competent person
Lists the main items checked
Results recorded; tag shows safe or not safe with date and signature
Users check the tag every time; no tag or unsafe tag means do not use

essays.stem: Explain the precautions needed when welding or cutting from a scaffold platform, and why each is needed.
essays.modelAnswer: Hot work on a scaffold needs a hot-work permit if the Centre or site uses them. Timber boards, rubbish and nearby materials can catch fire, so the platform is cleared, fire blankets are laid over the boards and around the work, and a fire watch with an extinguisher stays during the work and for a time after it. Sparks and slag fall a long way, so the area below is cleared and barricaded. The welding return lead is clamped to the work itself, close to the weld, never to the scaffold, so that welding current does not pass through tubes and couplers, which could overheat them or give a shock. Leads are tied along the scaffold so they do not trip anyone. Gas cylinders stay upright and secured on the ground, not on the platform. Nobody welds or cuts the scaffold itself. After the work the scaffold is checked for heat damage before it is used again.
markingPoints: Permit, cleared platform, fire blankets and a fire watch with extinguisher
Clears and barricades the area below
Return lead to the work, never the scaffold, with reason
Cylinders on the ground, leads tied, no welding on scaffold parts
Checks the scaffold for damage after hot work

essays.stem: Describe how a trained team should dismantle a scaffold safely, and how the parts are dealt with afterwards.
essays.modelAnswer: First the team leader checks that the work is finished, all tools and materials are off the platform and the scaffold is tagged 'not to be used'. An exclusion zone is set up around the base with barriers and signs. The team follows the maker's instructions or the method, which is usually the reverse of erection, working from the top down. Guardrails are kept in place at each level until that level is being taken down, and harnesses are used where the rules require. Parts are passed down by hand from person to person or lowered on a rope, never thrown or dropped. Ties are only removed as the scaffold comes down to them, so it stays stable. At ground level the parts are sorted, cleaned and checked, and any damaged ones are tagged and kept apart. Good parts are stored on racks off the ground, and the area is cleaned up and the barriers removed last.
markingPoints: Clears the platform, tags it not in use and sets an exclusion zone
Works top down in reverse order, as the method says
Keeps guardrails until the level comes down; harness where required
Lowers parts by hand or line; removes ties only as it comes down
Sorts, checks, quarantines damaged parts and stores the rest

essays.stem: Explain how workers are protected from falling while a scaffold is being erected and while it is in use.
essays.modelAnswer: The first defence is to build the scaffold so a fall cannot happen. Guardrails, mid rails and toe boards are fitted on every open side of a platform, and the platform is fully boarded with no gaps. During erection, guardrails for the next level are fitted from the level below, or the maker's advance guardrail system is used, so the erector is protected before standing on the new level. Where this is not possible and the Centre's rules require it, the worker wears a full-body harness with a lanyard clipped to a strong anchor point that the plan approves, not to a toe board or loose part. Harnesses are checked before use. Access is by a built-in ladder or a tied ladder, keeping three points of contact. Workers do not lean over guardrails, climb on them or stand on boxes on the platform. A rescue plan is agreed in case someone falls and is held by the harness.
markingPoints: Full guardrails, mid rails, toe boards and boarded platforms
Guardrails fitted ahead from below or by advance guardrail
Harness to an approved anchor where rules require; checked before use
Safe access by ladder with three points of contact; no standing on rails or boxes
A rescue plan for a fall in a harness

essays.stem: Compare a ladder, a mobile tower and a fixed frame scaffold as ways to reach welding work at height. Say which is best for which kind of job.
essays.modelAnswer: A ladder is quick to set up and cheap, but it gives only one point to stand on and the worker needs one hand to hold on. It suits short, light tasks such as a quick look or a measurement, not welding, which needs both hands, a helmet and a steady stance. A mobile tower gives a guarded platform for one or two people and their tools, and can be moved between jobs once everyone is off it. It needs firm, level ground and must stay inside the maker's height limit. It suits welding brackets on columns or pipe supports inside the shop. A fixed frame scaffold takes longer to put up and needs ties, but it can be long and high, carry more load and stay in place for days. It suits long runs of welding, such as a canopy or a tank, outdoors. For any of them, the choice is made in the plan, and towers and scaffolds are erected by trained people and inspected.
markingPoints: Ladder: quick and cheap, but not suited to welding with both hands
Mobile tower: guarded, movable, needs level ground and height limits
Fixed scaffold: larger, longer jobs and more load, but slower and needs ties
Matches each to a suitable welding job
States trained erection and inspection for towers and scaffolds

essays.stem: Describe the site and weather hazards that affect a scaffold used for welding work outdoors in Jamaica, and how each is controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: Soft or uneven ground, made worse by heavy rain, can let a leg sink, so base plates, sole boards and base jacks are used, and the base is checked after rain. Strong wind, especially in the hurricane season, can blow over a tower or sheeted scaffold, so the maker's wind limits are followed, work stops when they are passed, sheeting is not added without advice, and towers are tied or taken down before a storm. Heavy rain makes boards slippery and can wash out the ground, so the scaffold is inspected again before use. Overhead power lines are kept well clear, and the power company and the Centre are asked for advice if a scaffold must go near them. Vehicles and forklifts can hit the scaffold, so it is barricaded and signed. Hot sun makes metal hot to touch and tires workers, so gloves are worn and water and breaks are planned.
markingPoints: Ground and rain: base plates, sole boards and re-inspection
Wind and storms: maker's limits, stop work, tie or dismantle
Overhead power lines: keep clear, seek advice
Vehicles: barricades and signs
Heat and sun: gloves, water and breaks

essays.stem: You lead a team of four trainees who will put up a tower scaffold, under the Centre's trained scaffold instructor, for a weld repair. Explain how you would brief, organise and supervise them.
essays.modelAnswer: Before we start I brief the team at the job with the instructor. I explain the task, the type of tower, the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules: only trained and authorised people erect it, and trainees work only under the instructor's direct supervision. I go over the hazards and controls: the exclusion zone, PPE, harness where required, no climbing on frames and passing parts by hand. I give each person a clear role, for example two checking and passing parts, two assembling, with one acting as the signaller so that everyone knows when to take and let go of a part. During the work I watch each step against the instructions, check the base is level and the brakes are on, and stop the work if anything is unsafe. I make sure no one uses the tower until it is inspected and tagged. At the end I record the inspection, report any faulty parts and ask the team what went well and what to improve.
markingPoints: Briefs the task, maker's instructions and the Centre's rules on who erects
Explains hazards, PPE, exclusion zone and harness use
Gives clear roles and agreed signals
Supervises each step and stops unsafe work; no use before inspection and tag
Records, reports faulty parts and reviews with the team

practical1.title: Plan, erect, inspect, tag and dismantle a mobile tower scaffold for a welding job
practical1.brief: This task is done under the direct supervision of the Centre's trained scaffold instructor, who must be present throughout and who decides the height (no higher than the Centre's rules allow for training). The assessor shows your group a welding job at height in the shop, such as a bracket position on a column. As a group, write a short access plan: the tower type and height, the base and outriggers, the hazards and controls, the exclusion zone, and each member's role. Check every part of the tower against the maker's instructions and set aside any faulty part with a tag. Erect the tower in the maker's order, with the castors locked, the base levelled, the outriggers fitted and guardrails in place before anyone stands on a new level. Fit toe boards. The group then inspects the tower with a checklist; the instructor checks it and the group fills in the inspection tag. One member at a time climbs the tower and marks the bracket position, and the group sets out the hot-work precautions (fire blanket, extinguisher, lead route); no welding is done from the tower unless the assessor directs it. Finally, dismantle the tower in reverse order and store the parts. Rotate roles so every member assembles, passes parts and inspects. Photograph each stage and add the photos, the plan and the checklist to the group's practical.
materials: A mobile tower scaffold with its maker's instructions, outriggers and toe boards
Barriers or cones and signs for the exclusion zone
Hard hats, safety boots, gloves, and harnesses if the Centre's rules require them
Fire blanket and extinguisher for the hot-work set-out
Access plan sheet, component checklist, inspection checklist and inspection tag
photos: The group's written access plan with roles
The parts laid out and being checked, with any faulty part tagged
The base with castors locked, levelled and outriggers fitted
A member fitting guardrails from the level below
The finished tower with guardrails, toe boards and the exclusion zone
The completed inspection checklist and tag at the access point
The hot-work set-out on the platform
checklist: Helped write the access plan and knew their role
Checked components and tagged a faulty part correctly
Followed the maker's order and locked castors and levelled the base
Fitted guardrails before standing on a new level and used the ladder correctly
Passed parts by hand and used the agreed signals
Inspected the tower against the checklist and completed the tag
Set out hot-work precautions correctly, with the return lead to the work, not the scaffold
Dismantled in reverse order and stored parts neatly
safety: Only work on the tower under the trained instructor's direct supervision, as the Centre's rules require
Wear a hard hat, safety boots and gloves; wear a harness where the rules require it
Keep everyone out of the exclusion zone while the tower is going up or coming down
Lock the castors before anyone climbs and never move the tower with anyone or anything on it
Never climb the outside of the frame or stand on guardrails; use the built-in ladder

practical2.title: Erect a frame scaffold bay on uneven ground with ladder access, inspect it for planted faults, then dismantle and store it
practical2.brief: This task is done under the direct supervision of the Centre's trained scaffold instructor, who sets the height (one or two lifts, as the Centre's rules allow). The assessor marks out a place on uneven ground in the yard and gives your group a frame scaffold kit, base jacks, sole boards and a ladder. As a group, plan the bay and list the parts. Check the components and tag any faulty part. Lay sole boards and base jacks, level and square the first lift, then build the bay with braces, a fully boarded platform, guardrails, mid rails and toe boards, and a tied ladder at the right angle reaching above the platform. When the bay is finished, the assessor plants three or four faults (for example a missing coupler pin, a loose board, a base jack wound out too far, a missing toe board). Each member inspects the bay with the checklist, finds and records the faults, and the group decides whether the scaffold may be tagged for use. The faults are put right under the instructor's eye and the bay is inspected and tagged. Finally dismantle it in reverse order and store the parts. Photograph each stage and add the photos and the inspection record to the group's practical.
materials: A frame scaffold kit with braces, boards, guardrails and toe boards
Base jacks, base plates, sole boards and a ladder with ties
Spirit level, tape measure and string line
Barriers and signs, hard hats, safety boots, gloves and harnesses if required
Inspection checklist, fault record and inspection tag
photos: The sole boards and base jacks laid on the uneven ground
The first lift levelled, with a spirit level in view
The finished bay with guardrails, toe boards and the tied ladder
A member inspecting the bay with the checklist
The planted faults marked or pointed out
The completed fault record and the tag on the bay
The parts sorted and stored after dismantling
checklist: Helped plan the bay and list the parts
Set sole boards and base jacks correctly and levelled the first lift
Fitted braces, boards, guardrails and toe boards correctly
Set up and tied the ladder at the right angle, above the platform
Found and recorded the planted faults during inspection
Took part in a correct decision on whether the bay could be tagged
